messages:
linda park: Heads-up — user forwarded an email that looked like a 1Password recovery. They clicked the link but did not enter creds (says they closed the page). Forwarded raw email and headers below. Can someone triage? :eyes:

sec-bot: New report logged (INC-4487). Running quick triage: static link check + sandbox detonation. Will post results.

maria g.: Thanks Linda. Can you paste the full raw headers and the exact link? Even a screenshot of redirect chain helps.

linda park: Pasting headers (redacted):

```
From: support@1pass-security.com
To: emily@redwood.ai
Subject: 1Password Account Recovery
Received: from unknown (HELO mail8.srvr)
X-Originating-IP: [203.0.113.45]
DKIM-Signature: none
SPF: softfail
Message-ID: <CAFk+abc123@mail8.srvr>

Body included a link: http://tinyurl[.]com/y-recover1 -> (redirect) -> https://1pass-recover.notify-verify[.]com/reset?token=xxx
```

maria g.: SPF softfail + no DKIM is a red flag. That domain is not our vendor. Good the user didn't submit creds. Jason — can you paste the sandbox detonation summary?

jason k.: Ran it in static + dynamic sandbox. Summary:
- Initial URL resolved to a redirector (tinyurl).
- Final landing is a credential-harvesting HTML form that POSTs to /submit.php on notify-verify[.]com.
- No binaries attached.
- Form captures email/password and has JS that exfiltrates to 198.51.100.22:8080.
- Indicators: domain notify-verify[.]com, IP 198.51.100.22, md5 of landing html: d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e.
- Sandbox flagged as phishing (IOC score 0.92).

jason k.: Uploaded detonation report to vault: https://inc-reports.internal/INC-4487 (restricted). :warning:

maria g.: Good catch. Containment plan: 1) Ask the affected user to rotate any company passwords they might have considered using on that page and confirm MFA still works. 2) Force a session revocation for their account (all active tokens). 3) If the user reused passwords on other internal services, rotate those credentials. 4) Search logs for any POST to that IP or domain from our corp network in the past 7 days.

tony infra: I'll run a quick query against our egress proxy logs and Cloudflare logs for outbound requests to notify-verify[.]com and 198.51.100.22. Also will check CloudTrail for unusual KMS decrypt events tied to the user's account just in case any secret exfil was attempted after click.

maria g.: KMS check is reasonable — if the attacker had creds we might see Decrypt/GenerateDataKey usage. Tony, prioritize Decrypt and GenerateDataKey events for the service principals the user can access.

tony infra: Started queries. Proxy logs show a single GET from the user's workstation to tinyurl at 09:12 UTC, then no direct POSTs from corp IPs to the malicious host. CloudTrail KMS logs show no anomalous activity for that user or related service accounts in the 24 hours around the click.

helpdesk-bot: Noted: password rotation request ticket created for emily@redwood.ai (TKT-10072). Sent user step-by-step to reset and confirm MFA.

maria g.: Nice. Next steps for closure: 1) Confirm user changed password + MFA confirmed. 2) Block notify-verify[.]com and 198.51.100.22 at the edge. 3) Add IOCs to our detection rules (proxy/EDR/IDS). 4) Run a quick inbox sweep for similar messages from support@1pass-security.com to see if this was a targeted wave. 5) Draft a short awareness blurb for product teams.

linda park: Emily confirmed she changed her password and verified MFA at 09:40 UTC. She also ran a quick check of her personal accounts; nothing else suspicious reported.

maria g.: I'll add the IOCs to create signatures: notify-verify[.]com, 198.51.100.22, support@1pass-security.com, tinyurl pattern. Also adding rule to flag emails with missing DKIM and SPF softfail from vendor-looking senders.

tony infra: Edge block pushed (waf + proxy) for those IOCs, started firewall rule to drop 198.51.100.22. EDR rule to watch for tinyurl->notify-verify redirect chains will be deployed tomorrow.

maria g.: Will open a short post-incident note for the security guild: timeline, IOCs, containment, recommended org-wide reminder. Assigning follow-ups: (a) detection rule owner: maria g. (b) comms blurb: linda park + comms team (c) training nudge: Security awareness team.

linda park: I'll draft the comms blurb and coordinate with comms. Suggest we avoid naming 1Password directly in the company email to not alarm and to focus on suspicious recovery links generally.

maria g.: Agreed. Final: mark INC-4487 as triaged -> containment complete. Will reopen if new indicators show up. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
